descripcion_geo: Coastal mountain range north of Israel, covered in legendary cedar forests. It includes the valleys of Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon.
importancia_estrategica: Main source of ancient Mediterranean construction wood; the cedars of Lebanon were used in the Temple of Solomon.

historias.titulo: The cedars for the Temple of Solomon
historias.descripcion: Solomon negotiates with Hiram of Tyre for the supply of cedars from Lebanon to build the Temple of Jerusalem.

historias.titulo: The Lebanese forest in love poems
historias.descripcion: The Song of Songs evokes the aroma of Lebanon as the fragrance of the beloved.

historias.titulo: Jesus in the territories of Tyre and Lebanon
historias.descripcion: Jesus retreats to the territories of Tyre, in the Lebanese region, where he heals the daughter of the Syro-Phoenician woman.

personajes.descripcion: He supplied cedars and craftsmen to Solomon for the Temple; commercial ally of Israel.
He used the cedars of Lebanon to build the Temple and his own palace.
He visited the region of Lebanon (Tyre and Sidon) extending his ministry to Gentile territory.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: The cedars of Lebanon symbolize greatness and permanence in the Bible; The region was the scene of the meeting between Israel and the Phoenician world.

judaismo.descripcion: The cedars of Lebanon are planted by God himself (Ps 104:16) and a symbol of the majestic and powerful.
judaismo.significado_teologico: The cedars of Lebanon are planted by God himself (Ps 104:16) and a symbol of the majestic and powerful.

cristianismo.fuente_primaria: Nuevo Testamento / Padres de la Iglesia
cristianismo.descripcion: Jesus visits the Lebanese region; The Syrophoenician woman represents the opening of the gospel to the Gentiles.
cristianismo.significado_teologico: Jesus visits the Lebanese region; The Syrophoenician woman represents the opening of the gospel to the Gentiles.
